# rtl-sdr

**Host tools and library for RTL2832U-based receivers**

- **Version recorded:** 2.0.2
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://gitea.osmocom.org/sdr/rtl-sdr>

## What it does

The command-line tools and shared library for RTL2832U DVB-T dongles used as general receivers: rtl_test, rtl_fm, rtl_power, rtl_tcp and rtl_sdr itself.

## Why you would want it

It is the foundation of the cheapest possible entry into SDR, and rtl_test is the canonical first diagnostic — if it reports your dongle and its tuner, the hardware and permissions are right and any remaining problem is in the application.

## Before it will work

An RTL2832U-based dongle and the udev rules from the rtl-sdr hardware entry, which now carries all 42 identifiers Debian's own rule recognises.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`sdr`](../profiles/sdr.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install rtl-sdr --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `rtl_test-tuner`.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `rtl-sdr`

## Known problems

The kernel's DVB-T driver claims the device first on many systems and must be blacklisted; rtl_test reports this as a device that is busy. Cheap dongles drift with temperature and need a PPM correction, which is not a fault. Several tuner chips exist behind the same identifiers with different frequency coverage.
